name: Gill Kennedy
role: Medora businessman; later ran an oyster restaurant
bio: Gill Kennedy (also G. D. Kennedy) was a Medora businessman who had a claim next to the Belfield townsite and made frequent trips there in 1884. That year he signed the call for the Republican county convention and sat on the committee that chose delegates to the territorial convention, and he painted the stage coaches and the company's offices, kept a clerk, and played banjo at local dances. In January 1885, while he was visiting Adrian, Michigan, fire burned the building he occupied, though most of his stock was saved; later that year he advertised cedar posts, found a limestone deposit near Medora that made good lime, and in September moved his building across the river to open a restaurant dealing mainly in oysters, adding an ice-house. At the April 1886 election he brought the election officers a pail of lemonade.
